create.name: Insight Meditation Community of Charlottesville
create.bio:
The Insight Meditation Community of Charlottesville, known as IMCC, has been sharing vipassana practice in central Virginia since 1996. It belongs to the Insight tradition rooted in the Buddha's early teachings, and presents meditation as open to anyone whatever their beliefs; one of its co-founders, the psychologist and Insight Dialogue teacher Sharon Beckman-Brindley, still teaches there. Teaching is planned by a Guiding Teachers Council and shared among a group of local teachers, with well-known visiting teachers invited each year to lead classes and retreats.

The main weekly gathering is on Tuesday evening at the Unitarian Universalist church on Rugby Road, with a guided sitting followed by a Dharma talk, and the same session is streamed on Zoom. Through the week, volunteers host short midday sits online, and smaller peer groups meet for spiritual friendship, families and socially engaged practice. The community runs classes, daylongs and retreats, and has built up an archive of several hundred recorded talks and meditations on YouTube. Its programmes are offered on a donation basis.

free_resources.title: Tuesday Nights: Guided Meditation and Dharma Talk
free_resources.description: A weekly evening of guided sitting and a Buddhist talk from one of the community's teachers, held at the Unitarian church in Charlottesville and on Zoom. Open to newcomers and long-time meditators.

free_resources.title: Virtual Noon Meditations
free_resources.description: Short lunchtime group sits on Zoom on several days each week, hosted by volunteer facilitators. Free, with donations welcome.

free_resources.title: Meditation 101
free_resources.description: Written step-by-step instructions for breath meditation, from settling the body and noticing mood to resting attention on breathing.
